body:
> **This is one of seven PRs split out of #38592.** That PR was +2105/−1366 across 41
> files, twelve of them attention backends on the serving hot path, and it interleaved
> hardening, a layout change and dead-code deletion in a single diff — a reviewer could not
> tell which hunk was safe-by-construction and which changed behaviour. #38592 is retained as the token-major
> layout PR (3/7), which is the core of the series.
>
> **Stack** — each PR is based on the one above it, and every one is green on its own:
>
> | # | PR | what it does | size |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 1 | #40326 | derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes | 21 files, +733/−118 |
> | 2 | #40327 | build paged KV views through one helper | 13 files, +704/−47 |
> | 3 | #38592 | **token-major layout** | 36 files, +1215/−1108 |
> | 4 | #40328 | mark the write loc physical and check it at every write door | 45 files, +935/−132 |
> | 5 | #40329 | remove the kernel-page multiplier plumbing | 17 files, +117/−230 |
> | 6 | #40330 | stride the KV translate kernel and route every translate through it | 11 files, +361/−159 |
> | 7 | #40331 | name the fused KV translate for what it computes | 28 files, +119/−121 |
>
> Review order is the table order. 1 and 2 are no-ops on today's contiguous pools (2 also
> fixes how HND pools with more than one KV head are read); 3 is where the behaviour changes
> and deserves the most attention; 4 adds the physical write-loc check; 5 is deletion; 6
> consolidates the translate; 7 is naming only.

# 3/7 — token-major dense views: a kernel-facing id IS the physical id

Base: #40327 (2/7). 15 commits, 36 files, +1215/−1108.

**This is the core of the series and the PR that changes behaviour.** The other six are
hardening, adoption sweeps, deletion or consolidation around it. If you review one, review
this one — and specifically its `layout-switch` commit.

## Why the layout has to change

Before, one page held a uniform array of row-blocks, one per layer per side:

```
page bytes = [L0_K * ps | L0_V * ps | L1_K * ps | L1_V * ps | ...]
```

Every per-layer view was contiguous, and the block origin was folded into its storage
offset, so layer `l` had to be addressed by a re-numbered id
`(t // ps) * (ps * blocks_per_page) + t % ps`. Views ran past the last page envelope, which
is what `view_tail_pad_bytes` sized.

That scheme is only valid **when every block has the same row width.** The old builder said
so itself, and asserted it:

> The page envelope `[L0_K*ps | L0_V*ps | L1_K*ps | ...]` is a uniform array of
> `2*layer_num` row-blocks **when K and V rows are equally wide**, so it is a valid paged
> pool under `kernel_id(t) = (t // ps) * (ps * 2 * layer_num) + t % ps`

```python
assert head_dim == v_head_dim, (
    "build_mha_views requires uniform rows (head_dim == v_head_dim); "
    "Asymmetric-KV models cannot use the unified pool (screened out at startup).")
```

One multiplier, one row shape, one stride can only address a page that is a uniform array of
equal-width blocks. Heterogeneous row widths are not *hard* under that scheme — they are
**unrepresentable**.

Now one slot's ENTRY holds every part of that token at a fixed offset:

```
page bytes  = [ entry(slot 0) | entry(slot 1) | ... ]
entry bytes = [ K_0 | V_0 | K_1 | V_1 | ... ]
```

so the per-layer view is strided with the entry as its slot stride and is indexed by
`page * ps + slot` directly.

### What that buys

Each part now carries its own geometry — `DensePart` has its own `row_shape`,
`offset_bytes` and `layer_stride_bytes`; `MHASubPoolSpec.entry_bytes()` sums `k_row_bytes`
and `v_row_bytes` **separately**. No uniform-row assert survives. `DenseEntryLayout.validate()`
checks that every part stays inside the entry and that no two overlap, and it requires
alignment instead of equal widths: every row, part offset and layer stride is a multiple of
16 bytes (the store kernels' vector width) and the entry a multiple of 32. A model whose
per-rank K, V or latent row is not a multiple of 16 bytes is refused with a `ValueError`
naming the row when the unified pool is built.

1. **Asymmetric KV** — the *layout* no longer forbids it. Startup still refuses such models,
   because the backends' read and write paths are not audited for it; what this PR removes is
   the structural obstacle, not the screen.
2. **More parts per entry.** A part carries its own row width **and its own count**, so
   further per-token state — for example a draft model's K and V as extra lanes of the same
   entry — can be added as parts without a new builder. Under a uniform-block page that is
   not expressible at all. Nothing in this series adds such a part.

### Three more consequences

- **No re-numbering.** `kernel_page_multiplier` is pinned to 1 (asserted, not read from the
  spec), and `translate_kv_loc_for_kernel` now computes what `translate_kv_loc` does. The
  plumbing that carried the multiplier is dead as of this PR and is removed in **5/7** — it
  is left in place here so this PR stays the layout change and nothing else.
- **No tail pad.** The views end exactly at the last slot, so the raw buffer is allocated at
  `total_bytes`.
- `entry_bytes()` is rounded up to `ENTRY_ALIGN_BYTES` in the switch commit rather than in
  the layout types, because it feeds `page_bytes()`, buffer sizing, the sub-pool anchors,
  `move_kv_cache` envelopes and PD transfer — the alignment has to flip together with them.

## The commits, and where to spend review

| commit | what | review weight |
|---|---|---|
| `layout-types` | introduce `DensePart` / `DenseEntryLayout` / `build_dense_views` alongside the old builders. No caller changes. | low — additive |
| **`layout-switch`** | switch `unified_memory_pool.py` to them: `layout()`, `entry_bytes()` alignment, `view_rows = num_pages * ps`, raw sizing, the sub-pool multiplier pin, the hook message, and the byte-law tests. | **the whole behaviour change lives here** |
| `layout-cleanup` | delete the page-major builders, the per-page offset and tail-pad helpers, and the id-space probe that the new layout makes vacuous. | low — pure deletion |
| `refuse trtllm_mha decode cuda graphs` | a startup gate; see *trtllm_mha* below. | low |
| `keep main's test edits` | the rewritten tests keep `main`'s `est_time` values and docstrings and do not bring back tests `main` pruned; the free `*_entry_bytes` helpers go, and tests derive the entry in closed form. | low — tests |
| `drop the pass-through CPU-copy overrides` | see #39477 below. | low — deletion |
| `describe the token-major entry` | help text, docs and comments that still described the layer-major page. | low — text |
| `import the paged-view helpers …`, `tidy the token-major layout code`, `take a part name and a slot count …` | follow 2/7's module move; `build_dense_views(raw, layout=, part_name=, num_slots=)`; comments. | low |
| `name the entry-layout module token_major` | `mem_cache/layout/page_major.py` → `token_major.py`, `build_page_major_mamba_views` → `build_mamba_entry_views`, and the Mamba view test after the module. Pure rename; the `--enable-page-major-kv-layout` flag keeps its name. | low — mechanical |
| `tag HiCache storage keys …` | see *HiCache storage* below. | medium |
| `refuse misaligned per-rank rows …`, `state the backend requirement …`, `keep the addressing rule in docstrings …` | the `ValueError` above; help text and docs that still said the Triton backends are required; shorter docstrings. | low |

## Interaction with #39477 (PD page-envelope transfers)

That PR added `_physical_to_kernel_indices` to both unified pool classes, re-numbering
physical ids by `kernel_page_blocks`. Under the token-major entry that formula is the
identity, so the method is removed together with the `get_cpu_copy` / `load_cpu_copy`
overrides that called it: the parents' methods take physical ids directly. Verified numerically on **both** pool
classes at page sizes 1 and 4, including the round trip and that neighbouring slots are
untouched. #39477's own SWA tail-allocation tests (17 CUDA cases) pass under this series.

The one upstream test that asserted the *scaled* form
(`test_swa_transfer_page_is_physical_not_kernel_scaled`) is adapted here to assert both
paths are physical, since the multiplier it pins is what this PR removes.

## Tests

The view tests are rewritten against the new byte law `byte(t, l, K) = t * entry + l * (k + v)`,
each cross-checked against an **independent (page, slot) description** of the same bytes at
page sizes 1 and 4, for uniform and asymmetric K/V rows. That independent description is the
safety net for the whole PR: the flat builder's addressing is verified against a second
derivation rather than against itself. `test_byte_addresses_match_envelope_formula` pins the
same law in closed form, independent of the builder.

## Validation

Model families exercised — a hybrid of every pool shape the unified pool supports, plus a
non-hybrid control. Perf covers the gated-deltanet hybrid (Qwen3.5-9B), the MLA hybrid
(Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B), the sliding-window hybrid (gpt-oss-20b), the tri-pool hybrid
(Inkling and Inkling-Small), and dense Llama-3.1-8B as a control. Accuracy covers the same
set and additionally the Mamba hybrid, Falcon-H1-7B. Each model is run unified against a
baseline on the same model, backend and configuration, so every delta isolates the pool.

Median inter-token latency, unified vs baseline: **+0.91%** (measured run-to-run noise floor
for this metric: 1.9%). Median GSM8K delta at n=200: **−0.25 pt** (binomial delta-sigma ≈ 3.0 pt).

Re-validated on the previous base (0318a8d0af) after review feedback: the stack tip (7/7) gives **+0.95%** median inter-token latency over 40 paired configurations (median per-configuration shift against the previous run of the same 40: +0.12 pp) and **−0.25 pt** median GSM8K over 26, with the full unit scope green.

The accuracy median excludes trtllm_mha with decode cuda graphs, which is refused at startup
for the reason given below; including it the median is −0.50 pt.

## End-to-end on B200

From this commit on, every allowlisted kernel reads per-layer views whose slot stride is a
whole entry. Besides the 2/7 kernel parity tests, each admitted SM100 backend was run with
unified memory against a baseline on the same model, flags and box (GSM8K 5-shot, n=200):

| model | backend | unified | baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-9B, tp1, cuda graphs off | trtllm_mha | 0.915 | 0.915 |
| gpt-oss-20b, tp1 | fa4 | 0.545–0.555 | 0.550–0.560 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2 | trtllm_mla | 0.900 | 0.900 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2 | cutedsl_mla | 0.900 | 0.910 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2, fp8 KV | tokenspeed_mla | 0.900 | 0.900 |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B, tp2, dcp2, fp8 KV | tokenspeed_mla | 0.910 | 0.910 |

trtllm_mha with decode cuda graphs is refused at startup under unified memory (below);
without graphs it decodes 9–13% slower than baseline, from the translate launches an eager
step adds. Not covered: fa4 on the gated-deltanet hybrids (fa4 cannot run head_dim 256 with a
paged cache on SM100, with or without this PR) and trtllm_mha at tp > 1.

## trtllm_mha decode cuda graphs are refused under unified memory

A defect that predates this series makes trtllm_mha decode under cuda graphs read
untranslated page-table columns: under the unified pool, the page table is refilled out of
graph before each replay, bounded by `cache_seqlens_int32`, which only the in-graph metadata
kernel writes — so the refill uses the previous replay's lengths. Measured: GSM8K
0.000/0.020 with graphs on against 0.900/0.900 with them off, baseline 0.905/0.900 in both.

Before this PR that configuration could not boot (its prefill path OOM'd copying a whole
sub-pool). This PR makes it bootable, so it also refuses it: `--enable-unified-memory` with
trtllm_mha as the decode backend and decode cuda graphs on fails at startup, pointing at
`--disable-cuda-graph` or another decode backend. trtllm_mha as the prefill backend only
still boots. The gate goes once the refill derives its lengths from the batch.

## HiCache storage

The unified host pool persists whole page envelopes. Their size does not change with this
PR, but their byte order does (layer-major → token-major), and storage keys recorded only the
model and ranks. Host pools now declare a `storage_format_tag`; `UnifiedPageEnvelopeHostPool`
sets one, and the controller appends it to the model name every storage backend keys pages
on. Pages written by an older build, or by a static pool, therefore miss instead of being
read back in the wrong layout. The page hash is unchanged, since it has to match the
router's.
